title: Design System: Abhishyanth Vemula — Portfolio V2

display.purpose: The name only: Unbounded 800, uppercase, masked lines for the entrance.

title.purpose: Interface titles and leads in Geist.

label.purpose: Mono identity marks, the Menu label, chapter meta lines and the scroll cue. Never prose.

action.purpose: Every button and text link, Explore included: IBM Plex Sans 500, sentence case.

editorial.purpose: Fraunces italic: chapter leads, personal asides and the closing line only.

shadows.name: case-frame
shadows.purpose: The only offset shadow: the evidence viewer frame lifting off the blurred page.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Default easing for state changes, reveals and cursor shape changes.

motion.name: pen-write
motion.purpose: Signature strokes: a pen that starts slow, travels, and lifts.

motion.name: signature-main
motion.purpose: Main signature stroke; crossbars 180ms and 200ms, the i-dot 80ms, 40ms between strokes.

motion.name: loader-min-hold
motion.purpose: Shortest loader hold on a first load; 0 when returning in the same tab or under reduced motion.

motion.name: loader-split
motion.purpose: The two loader halves parting along the seam; the hero is released at 1.3s.

motion.name: glyph-dwell
motion.purpose: How long the pointer must rest on a corrupted hero word before it decodes.

motion.name: cursor-shape
motion.purpose: Cursor dot, lens and caret transitions.

narrative.overview:
The site is a signed piece of work. It opens on warm ink with a signature writing itself, splits along the signature's baseline into a dimensional space, and carries one copper signal through every chapter: the hero's current, the network's pulses, the dot of the i, the focus ring. Everything else is ink, bone and a handful of low-chroma warm neutrals that give each chapter its own air. When a colour cannot say whether it is ground, type, a chapter tone or the signal, it does not belong.

The mood is cinematic, precise and human: title-sequence staging and engineered micro-detail, held in an editorial, print-like palette rather than neon. Density is deliberately uneven: the 3D world may be rich and layered, while the DOM interface stays sparse, quiet and exact so the person's name and the work always lead. The world is original; Marvel/JARVIS influence is energy and pacing, never copied props, reactor geometry, logos or HUD layouts. Rejected: violet, lavender and electric-blue light, cyan glows, neon halos, generic SaaS layouts, glass dashboards, noisy particle fields and a lone glowing sphere on black.
keyCharacteristics: Warm ink ground, bone type, one copper signal; chapters vary by low-chroma clay, slate, brass and olive.
A handwritten signature, not a geometric emblem, is the first thing a visitor sees.
Rich 3D world, quiet DOM: real HTML typography over a single WebGL canvas.
Depth from light and space, never from drop shadows.
Quiet and exact controls: bone pills and hairline underlines; copper only on focus, hover and live state.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Copper is the only saturated colour on any screen, and it marks signal or interaction: focus, selection, live state, the current. Never a field, never prose.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: Chapter identity comes from low-chroma warm neutrals (clay, slate, brass, olive, OKLCH chroma at most 0.08). Violet, lavender, electric or cobalt blue and cyan glows are retired everywhere: CSS, shaders, lights, canvas textures, favicon and social card.

rules.name: The Tinted Ink Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is tinted from the warm ground (Ink Tinted, Ink Muted), never a neutral or cool gray.

rules.name: The Name Wins Rule
rules.body: Nothing on screen, in DOM or WebGL, may compete with the display name. Holographic elements sit on the far side of the frame or behind a readability scrim. On wide layouts the camera measures the copy's right edge and frames the core so its outer ring stays clear of it.

rules.name: The Honest Mono Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is for labels and technical status, not as a costume for "technical" prose.

rules.name: The Counter Rule
rules.body: Counts and dates are data: IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures, the total in Ink Muted.

rules.name: The Selective Serif Rule
rules.body: Fraunces italic is for a sentence in the person's own voice, at most one per section. Lists, steps, specs and counters never use it.

rules.name: The Tight Tracking Rule
rules.body: Letter-spacing never exceeds 0.08em; wide-tracked mono reads as costume.

rules.name: The Made Object Rule
rules.body: If an object is meant to be a thing, it is built and lit like one: real construction, bevels, fasteners and physical materials. Unlit satin or additive "hologram" shading is for light itself, never for objects.

rules.name: The Light, Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: If something needs to feel closer, move it in space or light it; never add a box-shadow. Zero-offset glows are reserved for energy in the 3D world (core, current, pulses), never for DOM controls.

dos: Do keep the copper signal continuous: every new scene should receive the light from the previous one and hand it on.
Do keep copper to signal and interaction: focus rings, selection, live energy, the hover state of the primary action.
Do give each chapter its identity through a low-chroma warm neutral (clay, slate, brass, olive), not a new hue.
Do keep the loader honest: progress moves only on real checks, the full signature plays on every page load, and it enters on its own; never a mandatory click.
Do fit the hero (name, identity row, tagline) in one viewport from 1366x768 up, sizing with both vw and svh.
Do keep the name in real HTML at display size, with a scrim behind it whenever a scene sits beside it.
Do recompose layouts for portrait instead of shrinking the landscape frame.
Do give every holographic element an assembly state and a scroll-out state; both must reverse exactly.
Do ship a reduced-motion path that shows the fully composed hero without camera travel.
donts: Don't use drop shadows, generic glass cards, blurred panels, neon or copper glows, or gradient text.
Don't copy Marvel/Stark props, reactor geometry, helmets, logos or HUD layouts.
Don't let instruments or rings cross in front of the name on landscape layouts.
Don't fill large areas with copper or set body text in it.
Don't reintroduce violet, lavender, electric or cobalt blue, or cyan glows anywhere: CSS, shaders, lights, textures or images.
Don't put a geometric emblem (rings, rhombus, orbit) in the loader or the hero; the signature and the name are the entry.
Don't use ambient fog washes, wide glow halos or decorative particles; and never ship plastic-looking primitives as objects.
Don't give the cursor lag, a trail or a hollow ring.
Don't add eyebrow labels above headings or fake percentages to progress.
Don't use IBM Plex Mono for prose, Big Shoulders below 1.35rem, or Fraunces for lists and data.
Don't use more than one MCU line per chapter, put a quote in a heading, or reproduce Marvel props, emblems, portals or interfaces as visual nods.
